metrics.name: Code Quality
metrics.rationale: Source code content was not provided in evidence, but the modular file layout (config, server, service, store, modes, guard, auth, hooks) with clear single-responsibility boundaries and a passing test suite (32 passed, 1 skipped per README) indicates disciplined code organization. Cannot verify type annotations, error handling patterns, or style consistency without source visibility.

metrics.name: Architecture Coherence
metrics.rationale: Strong, coherent design philosophy: 'LLM is the router, server never thinks, modes as data.' Each module has a clear single responsibility. The data-driven mode system (modes.json to auto-registered MCP tools) eliminates redundant routing logic. The README explicitly documents and justifies architectural decisions (why no router, why JSONL not a database, why no sessions).
improvement_opportunities: Add a module dependency diagram to docs showing import relationships
Document the internal contract between service.py and store.py explicitly

metrics.name: Maintainability
metrics.rationale: Small codebase (10 source files in src/), 1:1 test-to-source module mapping, clear naming conventions, and data-driven extensibility (modes.json) make this highly maintainable for its scope. The design explicitly rejects unnecessary complexity. However, absence of CI and linting automation means maintainability relies on developer discipline alone.
improvement_opportunities: Add pre-commit hooks for formatting and linting
Add CI pipeline to automate test runs on push

metrics.name: Modularity
metrics.rationale: Excellent separation for a project this size: config, server, service, store, modes, guard, auth, hooks each handle one concern. Modes are data-driven (JSON), hooks are pluggable scripts, guard is togglable, auth is optional. The fire-and-forget hook design with mode-specific vs generic script resolution shows thoughtful modular extension points.
improvement_opportunities: Consider extracting a Store protocol/interface to allow alternative storage backends
Document module boundaries and their public APIs in a module reference

metrics.name: Malleability / Extensibility
metrics.rationale: Adding a new thinking mode is a single JSON entry in modes.json with zero code changes and auto-registration. The hooks system allows post-storage processing via dropped-in scripts. The guard is configurable via env vars. This is explicitly designed for no-code extensibility of the core feature set.
improvement_opportunities: Support hot-reloading of modes.json without server restart
Add a validation tool or schema file for modes.json entries to catch errors at edit time

metrics.name: Scalability
metrics.rationale: Intentionally single-serve and private by design. JSONL append-only with rotation (5 MB default) is appropriate for the notepad use case. No database, no in-memory reindex, no concurrent write handling needed. The design is honest about its scope ('not a transactional system'). Scored moderately because it handles its intended single-user load well but has no path to multi-tenant or high-throughput use.
improvement_opportunities: Document maximum practical JSONL size before read-back (journal) becomes slow
Consider an optional SQLite backend for users who need queryable history at scale

metrics.name: Security Posture
metrics.rationale: Strong security-by-design: no egress, no LLM calls, localhost binding by default, optional bearer tokens with actor derived from token (never from tool args), no secrets in hook payloads, state directory kept out of git. AUDIT.md exists as a dedicated security document. However, cannot verify auth implementation details or token handling from available evidence, and the GitHub license detection says NOASSERTION despite README claiming PolyForm Noncommercial.
improvement_opportunities: Publish AUDIT.md contents or link to them prominently
Add rate limiting for HTTP transport
Document token rotation and revocation procedures
Ensure constant-time token comparison in auth.py

metrics.name: Reliability / Resilience
metrics.rationale: fsync after every write ensures durability. Append-only JSONL eliminates corruption risk from partial writes. Log rotation prevents unbounded growth. Hook failures are isolated (fire-and-forget daemon thread, best-effort). Guard prevents agent loop abuse. The design is honest about hook best-effort semantics with a clear event table.
improvement_opportunities: Add write-error handling and retry logic for fsync failures
Consider atomic writes (write to temp, rename) for additional crash safety
Add graceful shutdown handling to flush pending hook tasks

metrics.name: Testability / Verification
metrics.rationale: 7 test files covering all 8 source modules (config has no dedicated test but is likely covered indirectly). README reports 32 passed, 1 skipped. The 1:1 test-to-source mapping is excellent for a project this size. However, cannot verify test depth, coverage percentage, or whether edge cases (rotation, concurrent access, hook timeouts) are covered.
improvement_opportunities: Add a dedicated test_config.py for environment variable parsing edge cases
Generate and publish coverage reports (pytest-cov)
Add integration tests for the full request lifecycle (call through to JSONL write)
Test hook timeout and failure isolation paths explicitly

metrics.name: Performance Discipline
metrics.rationale: The server does minimal work (template fill + file append), so performance is not a primary concern. fsync after every write is a correctness-over-performance tradeoff appropriate for a durability-focused notepad. No caching or in-memory reindex keeps the path simple. However, no performance benchmarks or profiling are documented, and journal read-back scans the full JSONL without indexing.
improvement_opportunities: Add a simple benchmark for journal read-back at various JSONL sizes
Consider optional in-memory index for journal queries on large logs
Document expected throughput for think_* calls per second
